lines.text: A-a-a... float it up!
Letters bounce like moon dust—catch each word before it drifts.
Look—A! Look—Astronaut! Astronaut drifts slow | trained for work where spacecraft go
B lands on Booster. A rocket booster provides extra thrust during an early part of a launch.
Capsule? Yes—C. Capsule small and round | crew or cargo rides space-bound
inside our soft moon-dust drift, the D clue is Dish Antenna. A dish antenna focuses radio waves so a spacecraft or ground station can send and receive signals.
Say E, then Eclipse. Eclipse slides through | one world blocks the light from view
Look—F! Look—Fuel Tank! A spacecraft fuel or propellant tank stores material used by an engine or thruster system.
G lands on Gemini Capsule. Gemini takes flight | two-seat capsule trained for lunar flight
Hubble Telescope? Yes—H. The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth and observes the universe above much of our atmosphere.
inside our soft moon-dust drift, the I clue is International Space Station. Station circles round | orbiting lab above the ground
Say J, then Jet Pack. A spacecraft maneuvering pack uses small thrusters for carefully planned movement in space.
Look—K! Look—Krypton Tank! Krypton stored just right | gas can feed an ion-thruster flight
L lands on Lander. A lander is a spacecraft built to come down onto the surface of another world.
Float the letter, land the name!
A to Z, our cosmic game!
Moon? Yes—M. Moon in view | sunlight makes its phases new
inside our soft moon-dust drift, the N clue is Nebula. A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust in space, sometimes linked to star birth or the remains of stars.
Say O, then Orbit. Orbit bends around | motion joined with gravity keeps the path bound
Look—P! Look—Planet! It is a large round world that travels in an orbit around a star.
Q lands on Quasar. Quasar, tiny gleam | giant galactic core with a brilliant beam
Rocket? Yes—R. It produces thrust by pushing exhaust in the opposite direction of travel.
inside our soft moon-dust drift, the S clue is Spacesuit. Spacesuit seals around | pressure, air, and protection space-bound
Say T, then Thruster. A spacecraft thruster produces controlled force used to change motion or orientation.
Look—U! Look—Universe! Universe opens wide | space and time and matter all inside
V lands on Visor. A spacesuit visor protects the eyes and face and can filter intense sunlight.
World? Yes—W. World in the frame | planet or moon can carry the name
inside our soft moon-dust drift, the X clue is Xenon Thruster. A xenon thruster uses electrically accelerated xenon ions to produce gentle, efficient thrust.
Say Y, then Yoke. Yoke turns left or right | hand-control clue in plain sight
Look—Z! Look—Zero-gravity Chair! A zero-gravity chair reclines the body for distributed support; it does not create real weightlessness.
Float the letter, land the name!
A to Z, our cosmic game!
Engines hush; one star keeps blinking. Now the answers come back from memory.
Look for A ... Astronaut! Float two hands slowly, then point to the astronaut.
Letter first: B ... answer: Booster! Lift one fist under the other like extra launch power.
C? Hold ... Capsule! Cup both hands into a compact capsule shape.
One clue—D ... Dish Antenna! Curve one palm like a dish, then aim it toward the sky.
Look for E ... Eclipse! Slide one round hand slowly in front of the other.
Letter first: F ... answer: Fuel Tank! Make a tall tank outline with both hands, then point only.
G? Hold ... Gemini Capsule! Cup both hands into a small capsule shape.
One clue—H ... Hubble Telescope! Make a long telescope tube with both hands, then look outward.
Float the letter, land the name!
A to Z, our cosmic game!
Look for I ... International Space Station! Stretch both hands wide, then trace one orbit.
Letter first: J ... answer: Jet Pack! Hold two hands by your sides, then make one tiny upward puff motion.
K? Hold ... Krypton Tank! Make a tall tank shape with both hands, then point.
One clue—L ... Lander! Lower one flat hand slowly until it lands.
Look for M ... Moon! Make a round moon, then turn one side toward the light.
Letter first: N ... answer: Nebula! Spread your fingers like a soft cloud of gas and dust.
O? Hold ... Orbit! Trace one clean circle around an imaginary world.
One clue—P ... Planet! Make one large round world with both hands.
Look for Q ... Quasar! Make one tiny bright point, then spread a big glow around it.
Letter first: R ... answer: Rocket! Point upward, then lift one hand like a slow launch.
S? Hold ... Spacesuit! Pat your shoulders and chest like a protective suit outline.
One clue—T ... Thruster! Point behind an imaginary spacecraft, then make one small push-back motion.
Float the letter, land the name!
A to Z, our cosmic game!
Look for U ... Universe! Open both arms wide, then hold the huge space around you.
Letter first: V ... answer: Visor! Shade your eyes with one flat hand like a visor.
W? Hold ... World! Make a round world, then hold it still in the picture frame.
One clue—X ... Xenon Thruster! Point to the thruster, then make one tiny backward puff with your fingers.
Look for Y ... Yoke! Hold an imaginary control, then make one gentle turn.
Letter first: Z ... answer: Zero-gravity Chair! Lean your hands back together like a reclining chair shape.
Float the letter, land the name!
A to Z, our cosmic game!
Float the letter, land the name!
A through Z—our space story lands on one bright final beat!
